races.verdict: The Flying Childers could be the key piece of form, with the third-place finisher FLANN SUNNA selected to enhance his positive profile and come out on top. In The Black has come a long way in a short period of time and given she was almost knocked over in that race, her performance can be upgraded. Mussab looks a solid 2-y-o, while Perfect Strike could have a bigger effort in him over 5f. FLANN SUNNA (IRE) IN THE BLACK MUSSAB

races.verdict: The vote goes to FORTY YEARS ON , who has proved most progressive in handicaps this season. She looks well worth another chance at listed level, with the forecast rain certainly no harm to her chances. Dance In The Storm again showed plenty of speed when fifth in the Ayr Gold Cup and is still relatively unexposed as a sprinter. She's feared most ahead of The Prettiest Star , who has some classy form, while fast-improving Zen Diva also needs a close look. FORTY YEARS ON (IRE) DANCE IN THE STORM THE PRETTIEST STAR

races.verdict: Having finished runner up to a next-time-out winner on her penultimate start, BINTOLA bounced right back to her very best when third in a C&D handicap 3 weeks ago. Leaving the impression she can do better again at this trip, Harry Charlton's filly shades preference over Lion of Mali who has enjoyed a highly productive season and wasn't seen to best effect last time. Miss Mambo has been knocking at the door and fitted with more severe headgear, she's put forward as the main threat. Captive Beauty and Ernie McCrew can fight out third. races.display_title: Copper Knight Winning-Most Horse Handicap
races.verdict: Having quickly bounced back to form when landing a small-field conditions event at Beverley 17 days ago, TOCA MADERA remains on the mark he's been competitive from in top-end handicaps this summer and may well be up to defying top weight eased in class. races.verdict: A good-looking renewal. The vote goes to COSMIC CONNECTION , who took his tally to 3-4 within the space of a couple of months in the spring and Chris Gordon's rapidly-progressive 5-y-o should have no issues with this longer trip. He can take the step up in class in his stride at the expense of Lord Byron , who was narrowly denied at Grade 1 level in Ireland and arrives fit from a spin on the Flat. Stable-switcher North Shore can get the better of La Cote Fleurie for third. COSMIC CONNECTION (IRE) LORD BYRON (IRE) NORTH SHORE (FR)
